name: Hong Sheng 洪昇
credit: No portrait available · Text: Chinese Wikisource (public domain)
bio: Hong Sheng (洪昇, 1645–1704), courtesy name Fangsi, was a playwright and poet of Qiantang (modern Hangzhou) in the early Qing dynasty. He spent long years in Beijing as a student at the Imperial Academy, and wrote a number of plays, of which Changsheng dian (The Palace of Eternal Youth) is by far the best known.

He worked at that play for about ten years and finished it in 1688. It was performed to great acclaim in the capital, but in 1689 it was staged during the national mourning for an empress, and Hong Sheng was dismissed from the Academy and ruined. He is said to have drowned in 1704, after a night of drinking, when he fell from a boat near Wuzhen. He is often named beside Kong Shangren, author of The Peach Blossom Fan, as one of the two great dramatists of the age.
